question: Which exact-target functions implement opendir/readdir/closedir?
prototype_hypothesis: opendir(path)->DIR*|NULL, readdir(DIR*)->dirent*|NULL, closedir(DIR*)->int, NuttX libc semantics
callsite_evidence: NSH procfs walker sub_C22848C calls sub_C1D50B0(path) to open /proc; loops sub_C1D5118(dir) until NULL to read dirent; calls sub_C1D50EC(dir) to close.
control_flow_evidence: sub_C1D50B0 allocates 104-byte struct containing file descriptor and calls open(/proc, 3073); sub_C1D50EC closes the descriptor and frees the struct; sub_C1D5118 reads 98-byte dirent buffer.
ownership_analysis: DIR handle is owned by caller between opendir and closedir; dirent returned by readdir is valid until next readdir/closedir.
unsafe_assumptions: STATIC_RECOVERED; d_name offset (+1) is verified only in the emulator
recommended_probe: List /data/app from Supervisor on Mirage and compare with NSH ls.
